quote: Colonies were led out to Sora and Alba. For the latter, situated in the country of the Aequans, six thousand colonists were enrolled.
notes: Six thousand colonists to Alba, four thousand to Sora, both on recently hostile frontiers.

quote: the heads of that conspiracy, after a trial before the consuls, held in pursuance of a decree of the senate, were beaten with rods and beheaded
notes: Frusinates fined a third of their lands for tampering with the Hernici; leaders tried and executed under senatorial decree.

quote: to quell this insurrection, Caius Junius Bubulcus was nominated dictator
notes: Dictator against the Aequan rising; triumphed and dedicated the temple of Health on the eighth day.

quote: Marcus Valerius Maximus was nominated dictator, and chose for his master of the horse Marcus Aemilius Paullus
notes: Dictator against Etruscan rebellion and Marsian seizure of the Carseoli colony lands; a variant in 10:5 has him pacifying Arretium by composing the Cilnian dissensions without battle.

quote: Marcus Valerius was elected consul, before the expiration of his dictatorship, many have believed, without his soliciting the office
notes: Irregular but consensual: sitting dictator elected consul in absentia by an interrex; Livy reports it as tradition (many have believed).

groups: plebeians of consular and triumphal rank
quote: the four additional pontiffs and five augurs should all be chosen out of the commons
notes: Ogulnian law opening pontificates and augurates to plebeians; debate Appius vs Decius spans 10:6-10:8; passed in 10:9 after a one-day tribunician protest, first plebeian pontiffs and augurs named.

quote: Marcus Valerius, consul, procured a law to be passed concerning appeals; more carefully enforced by additional sanctions
notes: Third enactment of the lex Valeria de provocatione, always by the same family; Livy explains the renewals by the overbearing influence of the few against the liberty of the commons.

quote: and two tribes were added, the Aniensian and Terentine
notes: Censors complete the survey and enlarge the tribal structure to accommodate new citizen territory.

quote: A colony was sent thither as a barrier against the Umbrians, and called Narnia, from the river Nar
notes: Strategic colony at captured Nequinum; explicitly a military barrier rather than a land-hunger measure.

quote: The dearness of provisions also distressed the state very much, and they would have felt the extremity of want
notes: Scarcity managed administratively: Fabius as curule aedile regulates the market and forms grain magazines (per the tradition Livy cites).

quote: An interregnum took place this year, the reason of which is not mentioned
notes: Constitutional gap of unstated cause; two interreges before Sulpicius holds the consular election.

quote: This year a colony was carried out to Carseoli
notes: Four thousand colonists per 10:3; planted in Aequicolan territory.

quote: he ordered that clause to be read aloud by which it was not lawful that the same person shall be re-elected consul within ten years
notes: Fabius invokes the ten-year iteration ban against his own re-election; tribunes offer statutory exemption; the centuries elect him anyway and he negotiates Decius as colleague — legality bent through ordinary channels.

quote: great numbers were prosecuted by the aediles, for having in possession larger quantities of land than the state allowed
notes: Enforcement of a statutory landholding cap by aedilician prosecution with near-universal conviction — direct evidence that a holding limit existed and was litigable in 298 BCE; key datum for the Disc I.37 land-tenure-register hypothesis.

quote: besought him to raise up the consulship out of the plebeian mire, and to restore both to the office itself, and to the patrician rank, their original dignity
notes: Patrician attempt to recover both consulships; Fabius refuses the illegal double-patrician return; Appius elected with the plebeian Volumnius instead.

quote: a sedition having been raised among the Lucanians by the plebeians and the more indigent of the people
notes: Class-based sedition in an allied state, suppressed by a Roman proconsular army to the satisfaction of the Lucanian nobles — not a Roman domestic event, included as Rome-managed allied unrest.

quote: the senate ordered the courts of justice to be shut, and a levy to be made of men of every description
notes: Emergency justitium with extraordinary enlistment categories (elder cohorts, freedmen's sons incorporated in the centuries) under the four-nation coalition scare; coded new-institution for the enlistment innovation.

quote: But persons were not readily found to give in their names; because they considered that they were being sent into what was almost a perpetual advanced guard in a hostile country
notes: Colonies decreed for Minturnae and Sinuessa; enrollment shortfall because sites were seen as garrison duty, not land provision — parallel to the Antium under-enrollment used in Disc I.37.

quote: This altar I dedicate to plebeian chastity, and exhort you
notes: Status conflict in the religious sphere: patrician matrons exclude a patrician woman married to a plebeian consul; she founds a parallel plebeian cult — institutional duplication as conflict resolution.

quote: the Ogulnii, Cneius and Quintus, being curule aediles, carried on prosecutions against several usurers
notes: Debt-law enforcement by fines, proceeds converted to public monuments; plebeian aediles the same year fined farmers of the public pastures — twin enforcement actions against economic offenses.

quote: the patricians endeavouring that Fabius should have Etruria for his province, without casting lots
notes: Inter-order fight over command assignment (senate allocation vs sortition); argued before the people and settled by popular decree for Fabius — Livy frames it as order-conflict more than personal rivalry.

quote: Quintus Fabius Gurges, the consul's son, having prosecuted some matrons before the people on a charge of adultery
notes: Morals prosecutions before the people amid pestilence and prodigies; fines fund the temple of Venus near the circus.

quote: by the support of three plebeian tribunes, in opposition to the protest of the other seven, and the declared judgment of the senate, he triumphed
notes: Consul triumphs against senatorial judgment and a 7-tribune protest, claiming popular will suffices; cites precedents of people-authorized triumphs — a constitutional collision resolved by raw assertion within split institutions.

quote: The ill humour in the commons was further exasperated, because the tax for the payment of the army was collected by contribution
notes: Fiscal grievance, not riot: Papirius banks all silver and brass in the treasury while the army-pay tax is still levied; contrast with Carvilius's donative the same year. Coded riot-tumult for lack of a grievance type; no violence.

quote: evaded, as was said, the jurisdiction of the people, by procuring the commission of lieutenant-general
notes: Tribunician prosecution of the ex-consul aborted when the consul's favor gives him a legateship shielding him from popular jurisdiction — an accusation channel blocked by office-holding.

quote: in consequence of some irregularity in their appointments, others had been, within five days after, substituted in their room
notes: Defective tribunician election corrected by prompt substitution.
